memory_candidates.content: A cp -al hardlink clone (e.g. dispatch-worktree.sh's .lake/ clone) shares the SAME INODE for every pre-existing file, not just disk blocks. Any ephemeral per-invocation runtime state file (lock/result/log/capture files) already present in a cloned directory becomes one file under two paths: a truncate-in-place writer in one tree silently clobbers the other tree's record, and a shared lock file serializes work across trees that should be isolated. Fix at the clone site by excluding the named ephemeral state files explicitly (never a wildcard), not by changing the state-file's own write logic. Record the hazard generically in the guard's own header (not phrased as a hard dependency on the specific cloning script) so it survives that script's removal.

When resuming an /orchestrate implement dispatch for a plan whose earlier phases were already committed, do not trust inherited phase-heading markers or pre-checked task-list checkboxes at face value -- re-verify that each phase's named target files still exist and still pass. A separately-tracked, concurrently-running or since-completed sibling task can delete or substantially alter a prior phase's target file between dispatches (observed: a worktree-isolation-layer-removal task deleted a file mid-way through another task's 5-phase plan touching that same file). When this happens, document the finding explicitly in the current phase rather than silently re-running stale verification criteria or silently marking them satisfied.
